narrative:
On October 17, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 52.3%, taking up 955 of the 1,827 scheduled matters across 46 benches. This reflects a notable efficiency gain over previous periods in the retrieved context, which recorded hearing rates of 44.6% on August 31, 41.2% on September 1, and 35.6% on September 3.

Individual bench throughput varied widely across heavy dockets. Justice R. Nataraj handled the largest single-bench docket, hearing 87 of 159 listed cases (54.7%). High efficiency on sizable cause lists was achieved by Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar, who heard 50 of 58 cases (86.2%), Justice Raghavendra Seetharam Srivatsa with 51 of 61 heard (83.6%), and Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty with 70 of 94 heard (74.5%). In contrast, high numbers of matters remained unaddressed in halls presided over by Justice C.M. Poonacha and Justice Suraj Govindaraj, where substantial supplemental rosters saw limited hearing activity.

By stage of proceeding, Orders comprised the largest single category and converted at 56.1% (345 of 615 heard). Preliminary Hearings followed at 51.6% (176 of 341), while Admissions saw a 47.4% conversion rate (256 of 540). Final Hearings reached a 39.6% hearing rate (55 of 139), a marked improvement over historical final hearing conversion rates of 19.6% on September 1 and 22.8% on September 3.

Case distribution remained heavily anchored in Writ Petitions (WP), which accounted for 801 scheduled listings with 390 heard (48.7%), followed by Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) with 193 heard out of 371 (52.0%). Regular Second Appeals (RSA) saw healthy progress at 56.4% heard (101 of 179), while specialized filings like Civil Contempt Petitions (CCC) and Civil Miscellaneous Petitions (CMP) cleared at higher rates of 70.5% and 75.0%, respectively.
